reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction from Ilya Sutskever in 2018. All three fixed searches ran, plus six more. The only forward-looking statement on a page I opened has no date or time span, so I've listed it under undated rather than as a candidate.

- **The undated line:** On slide 30 of his AI Frontiers keynote, given on 9 November 2018 in San Jose, he wrote that OpenAI had reviewed the past 6 years of progress, and concluded that "near term AGI should be taken as a serious possibility". I read this in the slide's alt-text on the Slideshare page; I couldn't see slides 41–52. Synced's news report of 13 November quotes him saying much the same words on stage.
- **Other pages I opened had no prediction:** An AiThority report on his late-2018 talk at NTECH, an internal NVIDIA engineering conference, only looks back at Dota and compute growth. A promotional profile from AI Frontiers has no quotes from him that look ahead. Only the opening 1.5 minutes of the GitHub subtitle file for his April 2018 MIT talk loaded, and they contain nothing about the future.
- **Things I saw only in search snippets, so I didn't quote them:**
  - **2019:** A tweet from March 2019 restates the AGI line as "should be considered as a possibility".
  - **2017:** An email excerpt says "Within the next three years, robotics should be completely solved". I believe it's from 2017, but the email archive page I opened stopped in 2016, so I couldn't confirm who wrote it or when.
  - **2018 emails:** One source says he emailed Musk on New Year's Day 2018, but I never saw the text.

I used 11 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
